class.name: WorldEnvironment4D
class.brief_description: Defines the 4D world's sky and ambient lighting.
class.description: A [WorldEnvironment4D] provides a [SkyMaterial4D] to 4D rendering engines. The cross-section renderer uses the material for the visible 3D sky and for ambient and reflected light. If the current environment has no sky material, the missing sky contribution is treated as black while [member ambient_light_color] can still contribute ambient light. If no [WorldEnvironment4D] is current, the background and ambient light are black. Only one [WorldEnvironment4D] can be current per [Viewport]. Unlike Godot's [WorldEnvironment] which extends [Node], [WorldEnvironment4D] extends [Node4D], which means it has a 4D transform. Rotating the [WorldEnvironment4D] node will rotate the sky and ambient lighting.

method.name: clear_current
method.description: Stops this environment from being current. If [param enable_next] is [code]true[/code], another [WorldEnvironment4D] in the same viewport may become current.

method.name: make_current
method.description: Makes this environment current for its viewport.

members.member: The color of ambient light in the scene not contributed by the sky. Only has an effect if [member ambient_light_sky_contribution] is less than [code]1.0[/code].

The ratio of contribution from the sky to the total ambient light, compared to [member ambient_light_color]. A value of [code]0.0[/code] means the sky contributes nothing to ambient light, with all ambient light coming from [member ambient_light_color]. A value of [code]1.0[/code] means the sky contributes all ambient light, with none coming from [member ambient_light_color]. A value in-between blends the two sources of ambient light.
If [code]true[/code], this is the current 4D environment for its viewport.

The material used to draw the sky and generate sky ambient lighting. Assign a [GradientSkyMaterial4D], [PhysicalSkyMaterial4D], [PlainSkyMaterial4D], or custom [SkyMaterial4D]. Rotating the WorldEnvironment4D node will rotate the sky and ambient lighting.

Adjusts the brightness of values before they are provided to the tonemapper. Higher [member tonemap_exposure] values result in a brighter image. See also [member tonemap_white]. [b]Note:[/b] Values provided to the tonemapper will also be multiplied by [code]2.0[/code] and [code]1.8[/code] for [constant TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC] and [constant TONE_MAPPER_ACES] respectively to produce a similar apparent brightness as [constant TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR].
The tonemapping mode to use. Tonemapping is the process that converts HDR values to be suitable for rendering on an LDR display.

The white reference value for tonemapping, which indicates where bright white is located in the scale of values provided to the tonemapper. For photorealistic lighting, recommended values are between [code]6.0[/code] and [code]8.0[/code]. Higher values result in less blown out highlights, but may make the scene appear lower contrast. See also [member tonemap_exposure]. [b]Note:[/b] [member tonemap_white] is ignored when using [constant TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR] or [constant TONE_MAPPER_AGX].

constants.constant: Linear tonemapping. Bright values are clipped, resulting in a possible loss of detail in bright areas. This is the fastest tonemapping option.

A simple tonemapping curve that rolls off bright values to prevent clipping. This results in an image that can appear dull and low contrast. Slower than [constant TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR]. [b]Note:[/b] When [member tonemap_white] is left at the default value of [code]1.0[/code], [constant TONE_MAPPER_REINHARDT] produces an identical image to [constant TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR].
Uses a film-like tonemapping curve to prevent clipping of bright values and provide better contrast than [constant TONE_MAPPER_REINHARDT]. Slightly slower than [constant TONE_MAPPER_REINHARDT].
Uses a film-like tonemapping curve based on the Academy Color Encoding System to prevent clipping of bright values. Slower than [constant TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC].

Uses a film-like tonemapping curve and desaturates bright values for a more realistic appearance. Better than other tonemappers at maintaining the hue of colors as they become brighter. This is the slowest tonemapping option. [b]Note:[/b] [member tonemap_white] is fixed at a value of [code]16.29[/code], which makes [constant TONE_MAPPER_AGX] unsuitable for use with the Mobile rendering method.
